headline: Switzerland, Rebuilt Block by Block
lede: This Minecraft world turns government geodata into a navigable country at true one-metre scale. Glaciers, forests, roads, and buildings emerge from a demanding pipeline of terrain data, procedural generation, and local compute.

headline: TitleArt Brings 1997 Back to the Browser
lede: TitleArt recreates the layered, tilted exuberance of 1990s web graphics in a small browser tool. Its keyboard-driven interface makes nostalgia tactile: select a layer, move it, rotate it, and remember when a school-paper title was a design project.

headline: PaperPilot Keeps PDF Workflows Close
lede: PaperPilot is a pure-Rust PDF engine exposed through a CLI, APIs, desktop software, WASM, and an MCP server. Files stay local or in browser memory while scripts and agents merge, OCR, sanitize, and transform documents without a cloud upload.

headline: Inside the NeXT Computer Office
lede: Stanford’s photographic archive opens a window onto NeXT’s offices, people, and design culture. These images preserve the setting in which a commercially difficult workstation company developed ideas that would later shape Apple’s operating systems.

headline: What Birdwatching May Do for the Aging Brain
lede: Research links birdwatching with attention, novelty, emotional engagement, and social contact—ingredients that may support healthy ageing. The evidence remains cautious: differences in experienced birders’ brains do not yet prove that birdwatching slows cognitive decline.

headline: Simple Rules Grow Surprisingly Convincing Trees
lede: A procedural tree model lets buds compete for light, distribute resources, and survive across simulated seasons. Later passes add thickness, sag, bark, foliage, and level-of-detail geometry, turning biological rules into varied real-time forms.

headline: 343 Million Books, Delivered to Children
lede: Dolly Parton’s Imagination Library mails one age-appropriate book each month to children from birth through five. The program pairs national funding with local partners, removing household income as a barrier to an early reading habit.

headline: Keybytes Makes Every Key a Module
lede: Keybytes turns a keyboard into a field of magnetic, individually addressable one-unit modules. Each key carries its own switch, RISC-V microcontroller, and power connections, while open schematics and firmware invite experimentation beyond conventional layouts.

headline: Overgrown Turns Neglected Tabs Into Gardens
lede: Overgrown lets abandoned browser tabs sprout animated plants until the clutter becomes impossible to ignore. A machete, chainsaw, or flamethrower clears the vines, making tab management a small, theatrical negotiation rather than an automatic purge.

headline: AI Can Draw Hardware Before It Can Build It
lede: Digital hardware design may yield quickly to AI, but physical products still answer to tolerances, vendors, factories, testing, and messy feedback loops. The harder frontier is not the drawing board; it is capturing the process knowledge that makes a design manufacturable.
pullquote: The hard part is not designing the object; it is making the real world produce it.
